messages:
maya: Quick pulse check — for internal service-to-service APIs, are we leaning protobuf/gRPC-first with an HTTP gateway, or keeping JSON/REST as the canonical surface? Asking because routing/quota/span propagation in the console needs a single source of truth.

alex: +1 to discussing. my vote: proto-first where it makes sense (internal high-throughput paths). but we need a clear adapter pattern for external REST clients.

ryan: Proto-first buys typing and smaller payloads. big caveat: browser + some infra teams will push back on gRPC.

samir: My UX concern: console rollouts + quota UI currently expects route -> verb -> metric. If we hide method names behind gRPC method descriptors, how do we show stable route names?

maya: Good point. Thinking: keep a logical routing contract independent of transport. e.g., route-id that maps to proto method or HTTP path. That way console, quotas, and telemetry bind to route-id.

iris: That sounds neat. question: who maintains the route-id mapping? service owners or a central registry?

alex: Prefer ownership by service teams; central registry (lightweight) for discovery + conflict detection. registry could be a small proto service with a HTTP admin UI.

ryan: Implementation note: Gateway adapters (Envoy + ext_auth + transcoder) can add a header x-route-id from proto annotations or OpenAPI tags. That keeps runtime routing agnostic.

samir: Can we rely on Envoy transcoder for all cases? Some payloads are streaming / bidi. Also, transcoder has quirks with complex oneof bodies.

maya: For streaming we fall back to json-over-ws or gRPC directly. But for most request/response routes, add an annotation in .proto like: 

```proto
// route_id: user.v1.GetProfile
rpc GetProfile(GetProfileRequest) returns (Profile) {
  option (redwood.route_id) = "user.v1.GetProfile";
}
```

alex: Love the proto option. tooling can generate an OpenAPI shim with the same route_id tags for REST-first teams.

ryan: Telemetry: ensure kube/sidecar + runtime capture route_id and method latency. Console should surface route_id with example proto signature.

iris: For quotas, we map quota keys to route_id + caller principal. That avoids churn when path changes but route_id is stable.

samir: Rollouts UX: need canary by route_id + model variant + traffic split. Console needs an obvious way to tie a rollout to one or more route_ids.

maya: Agreed. Plan proposal:
1) proto-first for internal services by default.
2) require route_id annotation in service protos.
3) central lightweight registry service (HTTP+gRPC) that indexes route_id -> transport mappings.
4) gateway adapters set x-route-id header for telemetry/quotas.
5) console ties metrics/quotas/rollouts to route_id, not transport.

alex: Quick checklist for POC:
- lint rule to fail CI if proto RPC missing route_id annotation
- generator to emit OpenAPI for teams wanting REST adapters
- envoy/transcoder example config for headers
- update console route model to accept route_id

ryan: I'll draft the envoy config snippet. expect small gotchas with grpc-web.

samir: I'll prototype the registry API (read/write/list route_id). keep it minimal.

iris: I'll mock console screens showing route_id-first views for quotas and rollouts — want to validate with a few product teams.

maya: Great. timeline: POC in 2 weeks? if yes, assign owners and we'll sync next Wed.

alex: I'm onboard. :thumbsup:

ryan: On it. :rocket:

samir: Taking registry.

iris: UX mockups by Fri.

deploy-bot: Deployed infra/proto-lint pipeline changes to staging (build-7862) — tests queued.

maya: Thanks — will set up a short RFC doc and assign PRs.

alex: One more note: fallback for teams that cannot switch quickly — support a proxy adapter that maps legacy HTTP paths to route_id via a static mapping file. low friction.

maya: Good idea. add as fallback in RFC.

samir: ack. will include mapping format in registry spec.

iris: I'll sync with platform-telemetry to ensure trace spans pick up route_id tags.

maya: Perfect. Closing loop: POC owners = alex (adapter + console changes), ryan (gateway configs), samir (registry), iris (UX/telemetry). I'll create the RFC now.

alex: Nice — thanks everyone. :clap:
